transcript.text: Samsung RS68A8820S9/EU flashing 22E on the display and the fridge side isn't as cold as it should be. What does 22E mean and can I fix it?

I can't confirm what 22E means on your model, so I'll go by what it is doing. From what you have described, the most likely cause is the fan or air channel that moves cold air into the fridge. Is the freezer still cold while the fridge is warm, and is there a thick block of ice on the back wall inside the freezer?

Yes, the freezer side is fine and the fridge is at 9C. I haven't checked the freezer back wall for ice - there's a bit of frost around the vent at the top back of the fridge though. No burning smell or tripping, by the way.
From what you have described, the most likely cause is the automatic defrost system. When you press the freezer door switch, do you hear the fan running, and are the coils clear or iced up?

I'm not sure about the freezer door switch fan - I haven't checked that. There's an occasional ticking/scraping sound from inside the fridge back panel, and the airflow from the fridge vents is very weak. I can't see any coils, they're not visible from inside.
Behind the rear panel inside the freezer, are the coils a solid block of ice, or fairly clear?
I can't remove the inner back panel so I can't see the coils, and I haven't looked at the freezer back wall. Is there a way to check without taking panels off?

No, you cannot effectively diagnose this fault without removing panels because the internal components are hidden. The weak airflow and error code suggest an issue with the fan or evaporator coils located behind the inner back panel. Cold air comes in through vents, often on the back wall inside. Make sure food isn't pressed against them and the shelves aren't packed so tight air can't move. Were the vents blocked or was it over-packed (and have you moved things), or was everything clear?
The vents are clear as far as I can tell and the door seals are fine. I haven't moved anything recently and the fridge door wasn't left open that I know of. So what should I do next?

You need to check for ice buildup on the evaporator coils located behind the inner panel of the freezer compartment. If you find significant frost or ice there, it indicates a defrost system failure that requires professional repair. The first step is a full manual defrost: switch it off at the socket, move the food into cool bags, put towels down and leave the doors open until every bit of ice has melted, then dry it and switch it back on. Have you been able to do a full defrost, or is there no ice to clear?
I haven't done a full defrost yet. Should I do that now? I have towels and a hairdryer, and a cool box for the food.

It depends on whether you are referring to using the hairdryer or moving items, as neither is safe or effective for this specific fault. You should not use a hairdryer inside the appliance due to electrical and fire risks, and moving items will not fix the underlying issue indicated by code 22E. Ice in the bottom often means the defrost water can't drain away. At the bottom of the back wall there's a small drain hole — once the ice has melted, clear it gently with warm water or a soft pipe cleaner. Was the drain hole blocked (and is it clear now), is it still blocked or frozen, or was it already clear?

I haven't defrosted it yet so I don't know about the drain hole, and I can't see the back wall without removing the panel. Is the hairdryer a no, then? Should I do the full defrost with the doors open, or is this something I need to get an engineer in for?

Do not use a hairdryer as it can damage plastic components and void warranties. You should perform a full manual defrost by leaving both doors open for 24 hours to clear any hidden ice blockages. Run it as normal with the doors shut for a few days. Has the frost started to build up again, or is it staying clear?

I haven't done the defrost yet, so I can't say whether the frost comes back. The only frost I've seen is a bit around the vent at the top back of the fridge. I'll do the 24 hour defrost with the doors open and the food in the cool box, without the hairdryer.
Keep both doors shut for about 24 hours (only open them briefly) and let it recover. After a day with the doors shut, is it back to cold, or still warm?
